about.header: I'm an offensive security Student based in Rabat, Morocco. The job is easy to describe and hard to do: get in the way a real attacker would, prove what it costs, then hand over the exact path so it can be closed for good.
about.bio: Three years across red teaming, Active Directory exploitation and web application security — backed by certifications from Hack The Box, Altered Security and webverse Labs. Engagements are mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, so findings read as attack chains a defender can act on, not a scanner dump. Currently completing an engineering degree in cybersecurity at Ensa Tetouan — and publishing a full write-up for everything I take apart.
focus: Active Directory attack paths in multi-domain forests
Adversary simulation mapped to MITRE ATT&CK
Chained web exploitation — auth bypass to RCE

projects.title: adpath — AD Attack-Path Enumerator
projects.description: Lightweight LDAP enumerator that collects users, groups, ACLs and delegation settings, then flags Kerberoastable accounts and shortest paths to Domain Admins. Exports BloodHound-compatible JSON.

projects.title: reconchain — Web Recon Pipeline
projects.description: Chained subdomain discovery, HTTP probing, content discovery and screenshotting into a single reproducible pipeline with deduplicated, triage-ready output.

projects.title: jwt-breaker — Burp Auth Fuzzer
projects.description: Burp Suite extension that mutates JWTs and session tokens (alg confusion, kid injection, weak secrets) to surface authentication bypasses during manual testing.
